south.description: To the south lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10771.description:
A broad floe drifts past here with the snow on its back stained a
curious pink, as though someone had spilled watered wine across it, and
the stain smells faintly of melon. Sailors' tales say it is a weed that
grows in snow. The floe turns slowly, and open water lies beyond it on
every side.

10772.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

south.description: To the south lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10772.description:
The water here is clear enough to show a great spur of ice reaching out
beneath the surface from a nearby berg, pale green and ghostly, close
enough under the keel to make you hold your breath. Above the waterline
the berg looks harmless, a low white hump. Open water leads away from it
north, east, south and west.

10773.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

south.description: To the south lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10773.description:
A slow whirlpool turns here, wide as a threshing floor, where the
current curling out from the strait meets the swell, and slush rides
round and round it in a lazy grey spiral. The boat swings gently with it
unless you pull clear. East stands the last pale bend of the Ice Wall,
and south the edge of the shelf lies low and white. North and west, the
sea is open.

10774.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

south.description: To the south lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10774.description:
The Ice Wall begins to bend away here, and south, beyond its end, two
icebergs stand so close together that only a thread of dark water runs
between them. The swell slackens in their shelter, and the sea turns
smooth and heavy, like cold oil. North, the wall marches back toward the
cape, and west the Southern Mira Retrum opens out among drifting floes.

10775.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10775.description:
This is a dead end of grey water, hemmed in where the pack ice and the
ice shelf have frozen together into one white, broken wall. The ice here
is silent, gripped so tight it cannot move, and the stillness weighs on
you. The only ways out are north along the edge of the pack, or east
beside the shelf.

10776.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10776.description:
The edge of the ice shelf runs here into the pack ice, and the two have
heaved each other up into a chaos of tilted blocks and shattered slabs,
some standing on end like gravestones. Nothing could find a way through
that. Open water lies back to the north; east the shelf's white cliff
runs on, and west a last pocket of water lies hemmed in by the ice.

10777.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10777.description:
An iron stake has been driven into the face of the ice shelf here, just
above the waterline, its head rusted to a lump and a few strands of
frayed rope still knotted around it, where some boat once moored against
the ice. Above it the shelf rises in a sheer white cliff. The shelf's
edge runs east and west, and north the floes drift on open water.

10778.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10778.description:
The edge of the ice shelf has been undercut here into a long overhang,
and from its lip hang icicles as long as spears, dripping steadily into
the shadowed water beneath. Far back under the overhang the sea gurgles
in the dark. It looks ready to fall at any moment. The shelf runs east
and west, and north lies open water.

10779.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10779.description:
From here you can see over the lip of the ice shelf to its top, a plain
of snow as level as a frozen lake that runs on and on until it melts
into the white sky. Wind sweeps loose snow off its edge in long, smoking
plumes that drift down over the water. The shelf's cliff runs east and
west, and north the sea lies open.

10780.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10780.description:
A great slab has broken away from the ice shelf here, and the new face
is raw and startlingly blue, sheer as a cut loaf, with water still
streaming down it. The fallen piece floats a little way off as a new
iceberg, rocking as it settles, and the sea between is choked with
shattered ice. The shelf's edge runs on east and west, and north the
floes drift in open water.

10781.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10781.description:
The sea has gnawed a cave into the ice shelf here, a low dark mouth
fringed with icicles like the teeth of some great beast, and each swell
that runs into it comes out again as a deep, wet growl. Spray has frozen
in fans across the shelf's white face. The shelf runs on east and west,
and north lies open water.

10782.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10782.description:
A long rift splits the edge of the ice shelf here, a blue chasm too
narrow for any boat, its walls hung with icicles and its depths lost in
shadow. The swell runs into it and comes back with a hollow sigh. The
shelf's white cliff runs on east and west, and to the north the open sea
is scattered with floes.

10783.name: The Southern Mira Retrum

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

east.description: To the east lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10783.description:
The edge of the ice shelf runs along here as a low white cliff, flat-
topped and level as a table, with the sea chewing caves into its foot.
East, two icebergs crowd close together, and a narrow strait opens
between them. The water is calm in the lee of the shelf and scattered
with brash. North and west, the open sea stretches away among drifting
floes.

10784.name: A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

south.description: To the south lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10784.description:
Two icebergs crowd together here, one leaning against the very end of
the Ice Wall and the other grounded on the edge of the ice shelf, and
between them a narrow strait runs south, scarcely wider than two boats
side by side. Their flanks rise sheer and dripping, and the light
between them is blue and dim. North, the water widens back along the
wall; west, it runs out beside the edge of the shelf.

10785.name: A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs

north.description: To the north lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

east.description: To the east lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

10785.description:
The strait turns here between walls of ice so high and close that only a
crooked ribbon of grey sky shows overhead. Every sound comes back
doubled: the drip of meltwater, the knock of the oars, your own breath.
The black water is perfectly still, and cold rises from it like a mist.
North, the strait leads back toward open sea; east it bends on around
the iceberg's foot.

10786.name: A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs

south.description: To the south lies The Quiet Bay beyond the Ice Wall.

west.description: To the west lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

10786.description:
The strait widens at last, and the walls of ice fall back to show,
south, a sheltered bay lying calm beyond the end of the Ice Wall, its
shore pale with shingle and snow. Beside you the iceberg leans close,
streaming with meltwater. The air is suddenly still, as though the wind
could not find its way in. West, the strait winds back between the
icebergs.

10787.name: The Quiet Bay beyond the Ice Wall

north.description: To the north lies A Narrow Strait between two Icebergs.

10787.description:
A crescent of grey shingle curves around still water here, sheltered on
every side, and over the bay the Ice Wall rises like the edge of the
world, blue in its hollows and white at its crest. Moss and tufts of
hardy grass grow in the lee of the stones, startlingly green, and the
bleached ribs of a whale stand upright in the shingle to make an arch.
No wind reaches this place, and the silence rings in your ears. North, a
narrow strait leads back between two icebergs to the sea.

extra_descs.whale ribs arch bones:
Someone set these ribs into the shingle long ago and lashed them
together at the top with sinew, now rotted to grey threads. Scratched
into one rib are rows of tiny figures: boats, harpoons, seals, and a
long, coiling shape that fills the bone from end to end.

10798.name: Around Cape Voogk

north.description: To the north lies Cape Voogk.

east.description: To the east lies The South-Eastern Mira Retrum.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10798.description:
Here the boat rounds the foot of Cape Voogk, where the black rock
plunges into the sea and the Ice Wall begins, grown onto the cape like a
white rampart taller than any tower. The current pulls hard along the
joint, swirling with slush. North, the water runs up to the point of the
cape; east and west, the seas on either side of it open out.

10799.name: Cape Voogk

east.description: To the east lies The South-Eastern Mira Retrum.

south.description: To the south lies Around Cape Voogk.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Mira Retrum.

10799.description:
The headland of Cape Voogk ends here in a tall black crag leaning out
over the water, its ledges white with frost and old birdlime. On its
very top stands a cairn of stones and whale bones, raised long ago by
someone who wanted this cape found again. The current races round the
point and heaps up short, steep waves that toss the boat about. East
lies the South-Eastern Mira Retrum, south the water rounds the foot of
the cape, and west it runs back into the Southern Mira Retrum.

extra_descs.cairn stones whale bones pole:
The cairn is a squat pile of black stones as tall as two men, bristling
with the bleached jawbones and ribs of whales. A pole on its top still
flies a few grey rags that were once red, and the stones at its foot are
scratched with tally marks and names too worn to read.

645100.name: seal grey
645100.long_desc: A grey seal lolls on a floe nearby, watching you with large, wet, dark eyes.
645100.description:
Its sleek coat is mottled grey and silver and still dripping, and its
long, whiskered face looks almost like a sad old dog's. It is fat and
clumsy on the ice, humping along on its belly, but in the water it turns
and vanishes as quick as a fish. A pale scar runs across its back where
something with teeth once nearly had it.

645101.name: penguin crested bird
645101.long_desc: A crested penguin stands on the edge of a floe, its yellow plumes ruffled by the wind.
645101.description:
It stands no higher than your knee, a plump little bird in black and
white, with a pair of shaggy yellow plumes sprouting over its red eyes
like eyebrows. It looks you up and down with grave suspicion and gives
an indignant croak. Its stubby wings are as hard as paddles, and its
hooked beak is sharp enough to draw blood.

645102.name: crab ice
645102.long_desc: An ice crab scuttles sideways over the stones, its pale claws raised and clacking.
645102.description:
Its shell is the size of a buckler, ridged and blue-white like old sea
ice, and frost clings to the joints of its long, spiny legs. One claw is
swollen far bigger than the other and looks able to crack a man's shin.
Small black eyes on stalks follow your every move.

645103.name: seal hunter man
645103.long_desc: A seal hunter sits in a narrow skin boat, harpoon raised, scanning the floes.
645103.description:
He is short and broad, his face burned dark by wind and glare, and he is
wrapped from crown to boots in sealskin sewn with sinew. A harpoon with
a head of carved bone rests across his knees, its line coiled neatly at
his feet, and a charm of yellowed ivory hangs at his throat. He gives
you a slow nod and goes back to watching the ice.

645104.name: killer whale orca
645104.long_desc: A killer whale circles in the dark water, its tall black fin slicing through the swell.
645104.description:
It is longer than your boat, a sleek mass of glossy black with a white
patch behind each eye and a white belly that flashes as it rolls. Its
fin stands up from its back as tall as a man, and when it opens its jaws
the teeth are as thick as tent pegs. It watches you with a cold, clever
interest that is worse than hunger.

645105.name: frost sea serpent
645105.long_desc: A frost sea serpent rears out of the water, rime crackling along its coils.
645105.description:
Its coils are thicker than a barrel and sheathed in pale blue scales
that glitter like ice, and frost smokes from its skin wherever the air
touches it. A ragged crest of fins runs down its back, and its long head
is armoured with bony plates, the jaws lined with glassy, needle-thin
teeth. Where it breathes, the sea around it skins over with ice.

745100.name: cloak sealskin seal skin
745100.room_desc: A sealskin cloak lies here in a sleek grey heap.
745100.description: A heavy cloak of grey sealskin, the fur turned outward to shed the spray and the seams sewn tight with sinew so that no wind finds its way through. It smells faintly of fish oil and smoke.

745101.name: charm walrus ivory amulet
745101.room_desc: A small charm of yellowed ivory lies here on a leather thong.
745101.description: A piece of walrus tusk carved into a curled-up seal, worn smooth and yellow by years of handling and hung on a thong of plaited hide. The seal hunters say it keeps the sea from taking you, so long as you never take it off.

745102.name: harpoon bone spear
745102.room_desc: A harpoon with a head of carved bone lies here.
745102.description: A stout shaft of driftwood as long as a man, tipped with a barbed head of carved whalebone lashed on with sinew. A loop of line is knotted below the head, and the shaft is worn smooth where a hunter's hand has gripped it.

745103.name: tooth killer whale orca
745103.room_desc: A great curved tooth, creamy white, lies here.
745103.description: A conical tooth as long as your palm and as thick as a thumb, creamy white and ringed with faint bands like the rings of a tree. Carvers and charm-makers prize them, and the seal hunters count one worth a whole season's catch.

745104.name: pearl frost
745104.room_desc: A pale blue pearl lies here, rimed with frost.
745104.description: A pearl as big as a thrush's egg, pale blue and cold enough to sting the fingers, with a thin skin of frost that grows back as fast as you breathe it away. They are said to form only in the gullets of the frost sea serpents, and any jeweller brave enough to handle one will pay a small fortune for it.
